assessment.completionStatus: Successful — all 18 scenario steps completed, including the conditional LLM extract step (DeepSeek key configured). Five independent extraction methods produced consistent product data; session state was saved and the reloaded detail page re-verified.
assessment.successRate: 95% — one transient silent-empty extract (fixed by retry) and one selector-discovery detour; every other step succeeded first try.
assessment.mostConfusingAspects: 1) htmlsnapshot inspect was the biggest surprise: tasked to discover selectors for the product title/price/description/image via `--max 3 --depth 2`, it surfaced only 'what repeats' patterns (recommendation cards, info pills) and never the unique page landmarks, and its scoped narrative emitted a misleading sentence about the scope selector repeating — I had to export the HTML and read it to find #productTitle / #product-price / p.description / #product-image. 2) DOM_FIRST_IMG returning "" for a straightforward #id selector with no warning — the silent no-match class of behavior is hard to diagnose. 3) extract --stdout printing {} with exit 0 on an empty LLM response. 4) The list URL column showing '-' for my active, reachable session with two live tabs.
assessment.mostValuableImprovements: 1) Let inspect list unique landmarks (headings, price nodes, images, id'd elements) or clearly point to summary/export for them; fix its scoped narrative. 2) Make DOM_*_IMG handle selectors that resolve to the img element itself (id/class) and warn on any silent empty image result. 3) Surface the empty-extraction warning on stderr in extract --stdout mode (or exit non-zero) so pipelines cannot silently consume {}. 4) Populate the list URL column so multi-session users can see which session is where.

issues.title: DOM_FIRST_IMG silently returns empty string when the selector matches the element without an explicit img tag

sections.body:
On http://localhost:18080/ec/dp/B0E000001 run an X-SQL query with rows FROM DOM_LOAD_AND_SELECT(@url, 'article#product-page') selecting:
  DOM_FIRST_IMG(DOM, '#product-image') -> ""
  DOM_FIRST_IMG(DOM, '.product-image') -> ""
while these all return https://picsum.photos/seed/1250857624/200/140:
  DOM_FIRST_IMG(DOM, 'img'), DOM_FIRST_IMG(DOM, 'img.product-image'), DOM_FIRST_IMG(DOM, '.product-images'), DOM_FIRST_IMG(DOM, '.product-images img'), DOM_FIRST_ATTR(DOM, '#product-image', 'src')
sections.label: Reproduction

sections.body: The documented "First image absolute src" should return the src when the selector resolves to an element (the id/class of the image is the most natural selector a user has), or fail loudly.
sections.label: Expected Behavior

sections.body: Empty string, exit code 0, no warning to the CLI user. The consumer cannot distinguish 'no image on the page' from 'selector shape not supported'.
sections.label: Actual Behavior

sections.body: The DOM_*_IMG family uses an img-scanning selector path: a selector without an explicit `img` tag token appears to be treated as a container whose descendant image is searched, so a selector that matches the itself (e.g. #product-image) finds no descendant image and silently yields "". This is a sibling of the known :expr silent-no-match behavior the backend already logs a warning for (HTMLSnapshotToolExecutor.kt), but the id/class case is not covered by that detection and the warning is server-log only. Engine parity fix is tracked upstream with the pulsar-ql dependency (per the code comment).
sections.label: Root Cause Analysis

sections.body: browser4-rest/src/main/kotlin/ai/platon/pulsar/agent/tool/HTMLSnapshotToolExecutor.kt (DOM_*_IMG warning path ~758-770, hasDomFirstImgExpr ~1039-1045); engine behavior lives in the X-SQL engine (pulsar-ql dependency)
sections.label: Code Pointer

sections.body: - Make the selector path return the matched element's (absolute) src when the selector itself resolves to an , regardless of whether the selector text contains the img tag - When a DOM_*_IMG call yields an empty result, surface a result-level warning (not just a server log line) naming the likely cause - Document the selector constraint in references/x-sql-dom-select-functions.md next to the existing :expr caveat, with the id/class example - Add a test mirroring the id-selector case alongside the existing :expr detection tests
sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement

issues.title: extract --stdout prints {} and exits 0 when the LLM returns no data — the empty-extraction warning is suppressed in raw mode

sections.body:
Step 10 of the scenario: run
  ./b4w.ps1 -s ec-eval extract "Extract the product title, price, description, image URL, and feature bullets from this product detail page" --schema '@.test-sessions/.../product-schema.json' --stdout
Observed: {} with exit=0. An identical retry returned the full 5-field JSON.
sections.label: Reproduction

sections.body: Either the empty result should carry a visible diagnostic (stderr warning and/or non-zero exit), or the command should be documented as 'exit 0 even when no data was extracted'.
sections.label: Expected Behavior

sections.body: Only `{}` is printed; no warning, exit code 0. Scripts piping extract --stdout into jq/CI see a valid-but-empty document and proceed. (In non-raw/file mode the CLI does print '⚠️ Extraction produced no data'.)
sections.label: Actual Behavior

sections.body: handle_extract computes detect_empty_extraction() (which deliberately treats "{}" as empty — there is a unit test for it) but the raw/--stdout branch prints the payload only and discards that flag; the warning text exists solely in the non-raw branch. The transient trigger was an empty LLM (DeepSeek) response, but the CLI-side behavior is deterministic whenever the backend returns an empty payload.
sections.label: Root Cause Analysis

sections.body: cli/browser4-cli/src/main.rs:handle_extract (~8650-8685, the `if raw { println }` branch); detect_empty_extraction at ~8727
sections.label: Code Pointer

sections.body:
- Print the empty-extraction warning to stderr in the raw branch (stderr does not corrupt stdout JSON), and keep stdout as pure JSON
- Consider a non-zero exit code (or an opt-out flag such as --allow-empty) so pipelines can detect the failure
- Include the retry hint from the non-raw warning in the stderr message
sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement

issues.title: htmlsnapshot inspect only discovers repeating patterns — it cannot surface the unique landmark selectors (product title/price/description/image) on a detail page

sections.body:
On http://localhost:18080/ec/dp/B0E000001 run:
  ./b4w.ps1 -s ec-eval htmlsnapshot inspect --max 3 --depth 2
  => reports a repeating pattern of .recommendation-card ('Customers also viewed' cards)
  ./b4w.ps1 -s ec-eval htmlsnapshot inspect "#product-page" --max 3 --depth 2
  => reports span.info-pill; the header even claims "The tool found that '#product-page' repeats as a sibling group" although it occurs exactly once
sections.label: Reproduction

sections.body: Per the scenario (and the inspect help: 'discover CSS selectors for recurring patterns' is the only described mode), a user on a detail page wants selectors for the main product title, price, description and image — the most important extraction targets on the page.
sections.label: Expected Behavior

sections.body: Only repeating sibling groups are mined; the unique landmarks (#productTitle, #product-price, p.description, #product-image) never appear. The user must fall back to htmlsnapshot export + manual HTML reading to find them. The scoped-narrative text is also misleading (claims the scope selector repeats, naming the wrong element).
sections.label: Actual Behavior

sections.body: inspect is implemented as repeated-pattern mining; elements with a single occurrence are not candidates by design, and the narrative/rendering labels the auto-discovered pattern with the scope selector's text, producing the misleading sentence. A new user has no documented pointer that unique elements require a different tool (the tool's own tip mentions 'htmlsnapshot summary' only for page landmarks).
sections.label: Root Cause Analysis

sections.body: cli/browser4-cli/src/main.rs:handle_html_snapshot_inspect (~10848; narrative strings ~11058 and 'Suggested selectors' ~11229); pattern analysis on the backend htmlsnapshot inspect tool
sections.label: Code Pointer

sections.body:
- Add a 'unique landmarks' section to inspect output (h1/h2 headings, price-like text nodes, images, elements with ids) with ready-to-use selectors, even when no repeat pattern exists
- Fix the narrative when a scope selector is supplied: name the actual repeated descendant (e.g. '#product-page span.info-pill (4 matches)'), never claim the scope itself repeats
- Document in `--help htmlsnapshot inspect` and the SKILL that inspect answers 'what repeats?' and that unique-element selectors come from summary/export/get probing
sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement

issues.title: list URL column shows '-' for active sessions that have open pages, contradicting the documented meaning of '-'

sections.body: ./b4w.ps1 -s ec-eval goto http://localhost:18080/ec/ ; ./b4w.ps1 -s ec-eval tab-new http://localhost:18080/ec/b?node=1292115012 ; ./b4w.ps1 list  (also list --verbose and list --json)
sections.label: Reproduction

sections.body: Per SKILL.md: 'list shows every session and its current page URL … "-" means the backend is unreachable or the saved session is stale'. An active session currently showing a page should print that URL.
sections.label: Expected Behavior

sections.body: Every active session (including ec-eval with two live tabs and freshly executed commands, backend_reachable:true) shows URL '-'. The column is effectively non-informative, so users cannot tell which page each session is on — exactly the problem the column is meant to solve when running multiple sessions.
sections.label: Actual Behavior

sections.body: Unknown — needs investigation. Either the backend session-status payload does not carry a per-session URL in development mode, or the CLI list handler does not read/populate it from the session's state (the session's last_access timestamp does update, so the state file is being written).
sections.label: Root Cause Analysis

sections.body: cli/browser4-cli/src/main.rs (list command handler / session row rendering); backend session status endpoint used by list
sections.label: Code Pointer

sections.body:
- Persist the active tab's URL into session state on every navigation/tab switch and render it in the URL column
- If the URL is genuinely unavailable for some session kinds, mark it 'unknown' in the docs instead of reusing '-' (which is documented to mean unreachable/stale)
sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement

issues.title: htmlsnapshot grep has no -o (only-matching) option and its error message does not list the supported flags

sections.body: ./b4w.ps1 -s ec-eval htmlsnapshot grep -o 'id="product-price"'
sections.label: Reproduction

sections.body: Either -o works (grep-standard, ideal for pulling matched substrings such as prices), or the error states that -o is unsupported and lists the valid flags.
sections.label: Expected Behavior

sections.body: Error: error: unexpected positional arguments (this command accepts 1): ["-o"] — a doubled 'Error: error:' prefix, no mention of which flags are valid and no --help pointer.
sections.label: Actual Behavior

sections.body: The grep option parser defines a fixed flag set (-e, -i, -n, -A/-B/-C, -v, -c, -l, -F, -w, --no-line-number, --selector, --selector-all) with no -o, and its unknown-token error path only echoes the rejected positional.
sections.label: Root Cause Analysis

sections.body: cli/browser4-cli/src/main.rs:handle_html_snapshot_grep (~11652)
sections.label: Code Pointer

sections.body:
- Add -o/--only-matching to htmlsnapshot grep (and top-level snapshot grep for parity), which is the natural way to harvest matched text like $899.99
- Improve the error to: 'unknown option -o; supported: -e, -i, -A, -B, -C, -v, -c, -l, -F, -w (see --help htmlsnapshot)' and drop the doubled 'Error: error:' prefix
sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement

issues.title: extract without --schema ignores the requested field list, despite the help example implying field selection

sections.body: ./b4w.ps1 -s ec-eval extract "product title, price, ratings" --stdout  (the exact example from --help extract)
sections.label: Reproduction

sections.body: Output shaped around the requested fields (title/price/rating), as the example 'browser4-cli extract "product name, price, ratings"' suggests.
sections.label: Expected Behavior

sections.body: A fixed generic envelope {"title": …, "content": <entire page text blob>, "links": […]}: the price and rating appear only embedded inside the content blob, not as fields.
sections.label: Actual Behavior

sections.body: Without --schema the extraction returns a fixed {title, content, links} document; the natural-language instruction only guides which text ends up inside content. The help's argument description ('What data to extract, e.g. product name, price, ratings') reads as if it selects output fields.
sections.label: Root Cause Analysis

sections.body: cli/browser4-cli/src/help.rs / cli/browser4-cli/src/main.rs (extract help text); backend extract tool
sections.label: Code Pointer

sections.body:
- Reword the help: '<instruction> guides what content to collect; use --schema to get named fields as top-level JSON'
- Make the first example schema-constrained (e.g. extract "product name, price, ratings" --schema '{"fields":[…]}") so the example's output matches its expectation
- Consider a warning when the instruction mentions commas/field-like lists but no --schema is given
sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
